normative_extracts.spec_section: HTML Living Standard §9.5 Broadcasting to other browsing contexts
normative_extracts.quote: A BroadcastChannel object allows scripts from the same origin in different browsing contexts or workers to send and receive messages on a named channel.
navigator.locks.request() grants an exclusive or shared lock for a named resource and releases it automatically when the callback's returned Promise settles or the tab terminates.

pipeline_phases: Automatic Lease Release on Tab Crash
engine_internals.mechanism_summary: The browser process maintains an origin-partitioned pub/sub bus and an async mutex queue that automatically releases locks if a renderer process crashes or closes.

production_failures.symptom: Duplicate background token refreshes racing across 5 open tabs and invalidating the refresh token
production_failures.root_cause: Each tab runs its own interval timer and posts refresh requests concurrently without cross-tab mutual exclusion.
production_failures.mitigation: Wrap the token refresh inside navigator.locks.request('auth-refresh', { ifAvailable: false }, ...) and broadcast the new token via BroadcastChannel.

production_failures.symptom: Deadlock when Lock A awaits Lock B in Tab 1 while Lock B awaits Lock A in Tab 2
production_failures.root_cause: Nested navigator.locks.request() calls acquired in inconsistent order across tabs.
production_failures.mitigation: Enforce a strict global lock ordering or use { ifAvailable: true } / AbortSignal timeouts.
